title: Sharp Joint Region for Off-Diagonal Transition Effects in Three-Alternative Dynamic Logit Panels
banked_reason: D0.5: incremental below the fixed field floor (paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4), not salvageable within scope; two local dual-normalization findings remain unrepaired and are disclosed.
gap_reasons: The general 30-atom formulation is a high-dimensional feasibility test without practical arbitrary-law bound computation or empirical use; Pakel–Weidner computable outer bounds are not engaged.
unnormalized-stratum-moment@thm:exposed-dual — K_r contains probability moments summing to one while q_r sums to w_r; the proof must apply the supergradient to q_r/w_r then multiply by w_r.
dependency-premise-mismatch@thm:joint-region — the theorem invokes normalized conditional relative interior but its dependency statement/proof does not establish dual existence under that premise.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived exact finite membership and support certificates, the b-axis point-identification elbow, accessible-support collapse tests, and rational nonidentification, nonrectangularity, and nonattainment witnesses. D0.5 judged these contributions incremental rather than field-level because the general-law method remained computationally implicit and lacked empirical implementation/comparator engagement. Two local normalization/dependency defects in the exposed-dual route remain unrepaired, so the banked note is a research artifact with an explicit soundness caveat rather than a clean theorem.
tldr: For the three-alternative, two-transition, constant-covariate dynamic logit with known stay multipliers and unrestricted alternative-specific fixed effects, the six population off-diagonal intervention transitions have an exact sharp joint region: 30 open-simplex atoms decide membership, 27 compactified atoms witness exposed maxima, and exact tests separate finite attainment from boundary limits. If either nonreference stay multiplier is one, all six transitions are point identified for every feasible history law; off both axes the generic relative-interior region has affine dimension three. Positive same-history twins, a rational nonrectangular projection, and a finite-effect nonattainment example show why the joint and boundary qualifications matter.
gap: Existing multinomial results identify staying probabilities or establish failure of universal point identification, while inspected sharp functional methods treat scalar effects. They leave the joint switching region at a given history law unresolved.
fill: Derive a finite atom/quartic certificate route for the actual unrestricted two-dimensional effect model, establish exact nonrectangular and twin examples, and classify law-specific point collapse and endpoint attainment.
